mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in a given month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, 20-day forward returns remain positive despite persistent FEDFUNDS > 5.25%, or the inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) does not exceed 3% during the same window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in employment growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL < 0.2%) predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market strength offsets inflationary pressures.
regime_hint: Labor market strengthening with deflationary inflation
failure_condition: Across 5 consecutive windows matching the trigger, the 60-day forward returns are not statistically superior to a baseline of neutral labor and inflation (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly rise in retail sales (HOUST) of at least 3% followed by a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 95 triggers a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals shifting demand toward services and away from manufacturing.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by ≥3% in month t AND INDPRO < 95 in month t+1
regime_hint: Demand-cycle shift from manufacturing to services
failure_condition: Over 10 such cycles, the 20-day forward return does not deviate significantly from zero (mean absolute deviation ≤ baseline SD).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 96 for three consecutive months) predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates a supply-side easing that may support price pressures and equity valuations.
failure_condition: Over 12 months, the 60-day forward returns during INDPRO contraction periods are not statistically higher than during expansion periods (Granger causality fails).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of UNRATE falls below 6%, the S&P 500 exhibits a positive 20-day forward return as lower real interest rates encourage risk-on equity flows.
failure_condition: During 10 such UNRATE declines, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4.5% in a month coinciding with a rise in consumer confidence (not available in catalog) is proxy-captured by a sharp drop in RSAFS below 400,000 triggers a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates overreaction in rate hikes.
regime_hint: Labor market tightening with risk aversion
failure_condition: Across 8 such triggers, the 5-day forward returns are not consistently negative (mean ≤ 0 with SD ≤ 1.5%).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent 2-month decline in GDP deflator (implied via CPIAUCSL < 101) without a corresponding rise in industrial production (INDPRO > 102) predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as deflationary expectations weigh on growth prospects.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 101 AND INDPRO > 102 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During 15 such deflationary windows, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a labor market expansion phase (defined by two consecutive months of PAYEMS > 210,000) predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate continued hiring and wage growth.
failure_condition: Across 8 such expansion regimes, the 60-day forward returns are not higher than the mean of all regimes (t-test p > 0.05).
